extraction_text: Janamejaya asks about the origin of the mongoose with a golden head that speaks human language.
Vaishampayana explains that the mongoose was originally the god Anger (Krodha).
The sage Agastva prepared milk for a ceremony to honor his ancestors. Anger entered the milk pot to test the sage.
Agastva recognized Anger and remained calm, conquering him through his ascetic power.
Anger was cursed by the ancestors to become a mongoose. The curse would end when he criticized Dharma.
The mongoose attended Yudhishthira's sacrifice and criticized him with a gift of flour, thus breaking the curse because Yudhishthira is an incarnation of Dharma.
The mongoose disappeared after the event.
Janamejaya asks how his grandfathers treated Dhritarashtra after gaining the kingdom, and about Gandhari's fate.
The Pandavas, after defeating their enemies, obtained the kingdom and ruled the earth, showing respect to Dhritarashtra.
